quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: A red light means stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops while driving.
Test your tire grip while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops while driving.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slowly on wet roads. To prevent skidding, avoid fast turns and stops.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.explanation: Only time will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a sharp curve in the direction the arrow points. In this case, the road curves sharply to the left. You may see several of these signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first begins.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slick film.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, how can you help other drivers see you?

options.text: Turn up your dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Use low beam headlights if your windshield wipers are on.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Keep your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share the same lane with a motorcycle. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use your inside rearview mirror.
Use your outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When can you pass safely on a two-lane road with traffic coming from both directions?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can reach the speed needed to pass.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-lane road if you can clearly see ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can reach the speed needed to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They alert inattentive drivers with vibration and sound that their vehicle has left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert inattentive drivers with vibration and sound that their vehicle has left the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger instead of the road while driving.
Only watches the vehicle ahead.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching for items, reading material, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instrument panel often. These safe habits keep you focused on driving.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give cyclists as much space as you can. Cyclists have less protection than car drivers and should not be crowded. Passing too quickly can knock a cyclist off course.

questions.question: A steady yellow light warns that the light will soon turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, move through as quickly as possible and clear the intersection safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash ahead.
Workers are on or very near the road ahead in the work zone.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very near the road ahead in the work zone.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the roadway. Drive with extra care through this area.

questions.question: When using roundabouts or traffic circles, you should:

options.text: Slow down as you approach the circle.
Yield to traffic, pedestrians, or bicycles already in the circle.
Enter from the right and steer left to go around counterclockwise.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a roundabout. Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the circle. Enter from the right and steer left to move counterclockwise around the circle.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main road.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, allow oncoming vehicles at least one-half of the main road. Both vehicles need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign is at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane, regardless of any other signals. You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before turning.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: To merge safely, find a gap large enough for your vehicle to enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with other vehicles?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Do not cross railroad tracks unless your entire vehicle fits on the other side.

questions.question: You should allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. Leave extra room to stop safely if the motorcycle brakes suddenly. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: This sign appears on roads near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and look for children.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your position.
Always stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When possible, make room to let vehicles merge into your lane safely.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Stay away from angry drivers. Avoid eye contact and gestures that might upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: You see flooding ahead on the roadway. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water may hide hazards even if it looks shallow. Turn around and find a different route.

questions.question: When may you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train sounds. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does excessive speed often lead to?

options.text: No increase in crash risk.
Better reaction time.
High-risk decisions.

questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decision-making.

questions.question: Must bicycle riders obey the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Bicycle riders have the same rights and duties as car drivers. They are part of traffic and share the road with other drivers.
